market_question: Will Marco Rubio win the 2028 US Presidential Election?
reasoning: The market implies a 14.1% probability that Marco Rubio, a specific individual, will win the 2028 presidential election more than three years away. Given the historically large field of unknowns (including many other GOP contenders and a Democratic nominee), the true chance for any single non-incumbent this far out is typically below 5%. Rubio's current role as Secretary of State does not materially elevate his odds above other plausible candidates, making the market price too high.
evidence_points: Presidential candidates this far from an election rarely have probabilities >10% unless they are a clear incumbent; the 2028 race is open.
Early 2025 hypothetical 2028 GOP primary polls show JD Vance, Ron DeSantis, and others leading, with Rubio polling in single digits.
Historical prediction market data shows that composite 'other' or specific candidate prices >1 year out regress sharply toward the field average.
sources_consulted: Early 2028 GOP primary polling aggregates (e.g., from FiveThirtyEight archives)
PredictIt and Polymarket historical pricing for equivalent far-horizon single-candidate markets
General base-rate analysis of individual candidate probabilities in open-seat elections
